title.es: Lo que dicen los buenos líderes

es: Reconocer en el habla de un entrenador si una frase es instrucción, ánimo o retroalimentación, y distinguir cuándo dirige y cuándo apoya.

teaching.en: A good coach will give instructions in short, clear sentences: pass the ball sooner and stay in your position.
teaching.es: Un buen entrenador da instrucciones en frases cortas y claras: pasa el balón antes y mantén tu posición.
teaching.explanationEs: Instrucción: imperativo directo que dice qué hacer ahora.
segments: A good coach will give instructions in short, clear sentences:
pass the ball sooner and stay in your position.
teaching.audioText: A good coach will give instructions in short, clear sentences: pass the ball sooner and stay in your position.

teaching.en: I love your effort today; you never gave up, and that is what will encourage the younger players most.
teaching.es: Me encanta tu esfuerzo de hoy; nunca te rendiste, y eso es lo que más animará a los jugadores más jóvenes.
teaching.explanationEs: Ánimo: reconoce el esfuerzo y motiva, sin dar órdenes.
segments: I love your effort today; you never gave up, and
that is what will encourage the younger players most.
teaching.audioText: I love your effort today; you never gave up, and that is what will encourage the younger players most.

teaching.en: Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in the second half, so that is what we should improve.
teaching.es: Tu punto fuerte es la velocidad, pero tus pases llegaron tarde en la segunda parte, así que eso es lo que debemos mejorar.
teaching.explanationEs: Retroalimentación: un punto fuerte + un dato concreto + algo que mejorar.
segments: Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in
the second half, so that is what we should improve.
teaching.audioText: Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in the second half, so that is what we should improve.

teaching.en: Keep going, you are doing great under pressure, and I want you to shoot as soon as you see the space.
teaching.es: Sigue así, lo estás haciendo genial bajo presión, y quiero que dispares en cuanto veas el espacio.
teaching.explanationEs: Ánimo e instrucción pueden ir juntos: Keep going motiva y shoot dice qué hacer.
segments: Keep going, you are doing great under pressure, and I want
you to shoot as soon as you see the space.
teaching.audioText: Keep going, you are doing great under pressure, and I want you to shoot as soon as you see the space.

teaching.en: The coach gave us some feedback after the match: constructive criticism names one concrete thing and ends with a next step.
teaching.es: El entrenador nos dio algunos comentarios tras el partido: la crítica constructiva nombra una cosa concreta y termina con un siguiente paso.
teaching.explanationEs: Feedback no tiene plural: some feedback, a lot of feedback.
segments: The coach gave us some feedback after the match: constructive criticism
names one concrete thing and ends with a next step.
teaching.audioText: The coach gave us some feedback after the match: constructive criticism names one concrete thing and ends with a next step.

teaching.en: Before the final, the coach gave a short pep talk that made everybody feel calmer and more confident.
teaching.es: Antes de la final, el entrenador dio una breve charla de ánimo que hizo que todos se sintieran más tranquilos y seguros.
teaching.explanationEs: Una pep talk es una charla corta para motivar al equipo justo antes de competir.
segments: Before the final, the coach gave a short pep
talk that made everybody feel calmer and more confident.
teaching.audioText: Before the final, the coach gave a short pep talk that made everybody feel calmer and more confident.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estas frases es una instrucción directa del entrenador?

choices.text: Pass the ball sooner and stay in your position.
I love your effort; you never gave up today.
Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late.

feedback.es: La instrucción usa el imperativo (pass, stay) y dice qué hacer ahora; las otras animan o valoran.

hint.es: Busca la frase que empieza con un verbo en imperativo.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tu punto fuerte es tu velocidad, pero tus pases llegaron tarde.»

feedback.es: Strength es el punto fuerte: la retroalimentación útil empieza reconociendo lo que funciona.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo de «punto fuerte»; empieza por str-.

origin.text: The coach did not shout at the team. She simply told Mia: Your ___ is your speed, but your passes were late in the second half.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Sigue así, lo estás haciendo genial bajo presión.»

answer.text: Keep going you are doing great under pressure

feedback.es: Keep going y You are doing great motivan; under pressure cierra la frase.

hint.es: Empieza con Keep going y termina con under pressure.

prompt.es: Escucha la charla del descanso y elige qué función tiene «I love your effort today».

choices.text: It tells her exactly what to change in the second half.
It recognises her effort without giving her an order.
It gives her a fact about how the game is going.

feedback.es: «I love your effort» reconoce el esfuerzo de Mia sin dar órdenes ni datos: es ánimo.

origin.audio: At half-time, the coach spoke to the players. Pass the ball sooner, she told Leo, and stay in your position. Then she turned to Mia. I love your effort today, she said, you never gave up. Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in the first half, so try looking up before you pass. The team was losing two to nothing, but nobody looked worried. Keep going, the coach added: you are doing great under pressure.

prompt.es: Con la misma charla, elige qué se le pide a Mia que haga distinto.

choices.text: To pass the ball sooner and stay in her position.
To shoot as soon as she sees the space.
To look up before she passes the ball.

feedback.es: La mejora para Mia es mirar antes de pasar; pasar antes y mantener la posición era la instrucción para Leo.

origin.audio: At half-time, the coach spoke to the players. Pass the ball sooner, she told Leo, and stay in your position. Then she turned to Mia. I love your effort today, she said, you never gave up. Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in the first half, so try looking up before you pass. The team was losing two to nothing, but nobody looked worried. Keep going, the coach added: you are doing great under pressure.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del entrenador con su función.

pairs: Shoot as soon as you see the space.
You never gave up today, well done!
Your passes were late in the second half.

feedback.es: La instrucción dice qué hacer, el ánimo reconoce el esfuerzo y la retroalimentación describe un hecho concreto.

pairs: Shoot as soon as you see the space.
You never gave up today, well done!
Your passes were late in the second half.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué actitud adopta la entrenadora con el jugador.

choices.text: She supports him while giving one clear point to improve.
She is disappointed and wants him to feel the pressure.
She wants him to stop shooting until he improves.

feedback.es: Elogia su valentía y su esfuerzo y señala un único punto concreto: apoyo con una mejora clara.

origin.audio: After the match, the coach sat next to a player who had missed an easy chance. She did not raise her voice. You were brave to try to score, she said, and your effort was the best in the team. The decision was late, though, so next time try looking at the goal before you shoot. Then she smiled. I want you to shoot again on Saturday.

prompt.es: Con el mismo relato, elige por qué dice «I want you to shoot again on Saturday».

choices.text: To give him an order about his new position.
To show that she still trusts him after the mistake.
To warn him that he will be tested on Saturday.

feedback.es: Pedirle que vuelva a disparar demuestra confianza: el fallo no cambia lo que espera de él.

origin.audio: After the match, the coach sat next to a player who had missed an easy chance. She did not raise her voice. You were brave to try to score, she said, and your effort was the best in the team. The decision was late, though, so next time try looking at the goal before you shoot. Then she smiled. I want you to shoot again on Saturday.

prompt.es: Completa: «Prefieren la crítica constructiva: una cosa concreta y un siguiente paso.»

feedback.es: Constructive criticism es la crítica que señala un punto concreto y propone un siguiente paso.

origin.text: Good coaches avoid vague comments like That was bad. They prefer ___ criticism: one concrete thing and a next step.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Levanta la vista antes de pasar el balón.»

answer.text: Look up before you pass the ball

feedback.es: La instrucción va en imperativo y sitúa la condición con before.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje del entrenador y elige con qué propósito lo escribe.

choices.text: To blame the players for being so tired after the match last night.
To give a list of orders for the next training session.
To give feedback that recognises a strength and proposes a next step.

feedback.es: El mensaje nombra un punto fuerte (correr), un dato concreto (pérdidas en el medio) y un paso siguiente: retroalimentación.

origin.text: Coach's message to the team: Good work tonight. I know you are tired. Your strength this season is how hard you run, but we lose the ball too often in the middle of the pitch. On Thursday, let's practise short passes. See you at six.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué quiere enseñar el entrenador con sus palabras.

choices.text: That clear, calm instructions help more than shouting does.
That players should never talk during training.
That only the coach is allowed to give instructions.

feedback.es: El entrenador sustituye el grito por frases claras y tranquilas: «Pass to me» en lugar de culpar.

origin.audio: During a training session, a young player kept shouting at his teammates. The coach stopped the practice and said quietly: Encourage, don't blame. When you shout, people get tense and pass the ball too fast. Next time, say what you need: I'm open, or Pass to me. Try it now.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sus comentarios nos mostraron cómo mejorar nuestros pases.»

feedback.es: Improve significa mejorar; la retroalimentación útil enseña en qué y cómo hacerlo.

origin.text: We were losing every game until the coach's comments showed us exactly how we could ___ our passing.
